text: What is the main function of the Central Processing Unit (CPU)?
optionA: To process instructions and control computer operations
optionB: To display images on the monitor
explanation: The CPU executes instructions and coordinates the activities of the computer.
subject: Computer Studies

text: Which part of the CPU performs arithmetic calculations and logical comparisons?
explanation: The ALU carries out arithmetic operations and logical comparisons.
subject: Computer Studies

text: What is the role of the Control Unit (CU)?
optionC: To direct and coordinate the execution of instructions
explanation: The Control Unit directs the flow of data and instructions within the processor and other components.
subject: Computer Studies

text: Which of these is commonly considered a major component of the CPU?
explanation: The ALU is one of the major CPU components, alongside the Control Unit and registers.
subject: Computer Studies

text: What is the purpose of CPU registers?
optionA: To hold small amounts of data and instructions temporarily for rapid access
optionB: To provide a permanent backup of all files
optionD: To connect a computer to Wi-Fi
explanation: Registers are very small, fast storage locations inside the CPU used during processing.
subject: Computer Studies

text: Which CPU component coordinates the movement of data and instructions?
explanation: The Control Unit coordinates instruction execution and the movement of data within the computer.
subject: Computer Studies

text: Which unit is commonly used to measure computer memory capacity?
explanation: Memory capacity is commonly measured in bytes and larger units such as kilobytes, megabytes, and gigabytes.
subject: Computer Studies

text: How many bits make up one byte?
explanation: One byte consists of eight bits.
subject: Computer Studies

text: Which of the following is the largest unit of memory capacity?
explanation: Among these choices, a terabyte is the largest unit of memory capacity.
subject: Computer Studies

text: Which type of memory loses its contents when power is switched off?
explanation: RAM is volatile memory, so its contents are generally lost when power is removed.
subject: Computer Studies

text: What is the output of an AND gate when both inputs are 1?
explanation: An AND gate outputs 1 only when all its inputs are 1.
subject: Computer Studies

text: What is the output of an OR gate when its inputs are 0 and 1?
explanation: An OR gate outputs 1 when at least one input is 1.
subject: Computer Studies

text: Which logic gate produces the opposite of its input?
explanation: A NOT gate inverts its input: 0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0.
subject: Computer Studies

text: What is the output of an AND gate when its inputs are 1 and 0?
explanation: An AND gate outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1; otherwise, it outputs 0.
subject: Computer Studies

text: Which logic gate outputs 1 when its two inputs are different?
explanation: An XOR gate outputs 1 when its inputs differ and 0 when they are the same.
subject: Computer Studies
